META.subject: Core Mathematics
META.titleDoc: CORE MATHEMATICS GRADE 10: INDICES AND LOGARITHMS
META.subtitleDoc: OpenAI-only evaluation • Sub-Strand 1.2 • 14 lessons • teacher review copy

UNIT.content: Indices; Logarithms to base 10; Application of indices and logarithms
UNIT.phenomenon: A fictional study chart says a negative index makes a negative value and every log method gives an exact answer.
UNIT.drivingQuestion: Why do we use indices and logarithms?
UNIT.coreCompetencies:
Learning to learn: the learner discusses in a group and generates the laws of indices.
Digital literacy: the learner reads and obtains common logarithms of numbers from tables and calculators.
UNIT.values:
Responsibility: the learner takes care of mathematical tables and calculators.
Respect: the learner appreciates the input of others while discussing in a group and relating powers of 10 to common logarithms.
UNIT.pcis: Life Skills – (self-awareness): the learner discusses in a group and relates powers of 10 to common logarithms and identifies the base.
UNIT.subject: Core Mathematics
UNIT.learningOutcomes:
express numbers in index form,
derive the laws of indices using factors,
apply the laws of indices in different situations,
relate index notation to logarithm notation to base 10
determine common logarithms of numbers from mathematical tables and calculators,
apply common logarithms in multiplication, division, powers and roots of numbers,
appreciate the use of indices and common logarithms in mathematical computations.

sections.title: 1. Index forms and factor-based laws
sections.prompt: Using CIL14,express0.001 as a power of10 and1/32 as a power of2. Derive3^2×3^3 and3^5÷3^2 by displaying/cancelling factors and state each law. Evaluate27^(2/3),4^(−1) and5^0 with root/reciprocal/quotient reasoning. State the positive-base or nonzero-base conditions used.
sections.exemplar: 0.001=10^(−3),1/32=2^(−5). Five factors3 give3^5=243;five factors divided bytwo cancel tothree factors,3^3=27. Same-base products add indices;nonzero same-base quotients subtract them. 27^(2/3)=(cube root27)^2=9;4^(−1)=1/4;5^0=5²/5²=1. Positive bases suffice here;zero/negative-power quotient identities require nonzero bases.

sections.title: 2. Inverse notation,table and actual calculator
sections.prompt: Convert both listed CIL14 power-of10 equations into common-log form. From the supplied log table determine log70 andlog0.007,showing signed arithmetic. Explain why0 andnegative inputs have no real common log. When an approved calculator is supplied,actually obtain log10(7),record the entry/full display,round to4decimal places and compare with the table;teacher separately records observation. OtherwisemarkNOTOBSERVED andleaveactualdevicecomponentpending;do not fabricate a display.
sections.exemplar: log0.01=−2;log1000=3. log70≈log7+1≈1.8451;log0.007≈log7−3≈−2.1549. 10^u>0 for every realu,so no real common log of0 ornegative inputs. Actual common-log7 display is model-specific,about0.8450980400 androunds0.8451;accept actual appropriate entry/display with observed action. Writtenanswers do not certify unprovided/unobserved digitaluse.

sections.title: 3. Multiplication and division by common logs
sections.prompt: Use only CIL14 tables to estimate7×5 and20÷8 by common logs. Show the log sum/difference,normalise any exponent,read the antilog andgive results to3significant figures. Compare with exact direct arithmetic and use≈where table values are rounded.
sections.exemplar: log(7×5)≈0.8451+0.6990=1.5441;antilog≈10×3.500≈35.0. log(20÷8)≈1.3010−0.9031=0.3979;antilog≈2.500→2.50. Direct exact35 and2.5. The exact log identities hold for positiveinputs;the displayednumericaltable calculations are approximate.

sections.title: 4. Powers,roots and a reasoned method choice
sections.prompt: Use CIL14 to estimate3² and√5 by common logs,showing the transformed log,inverse lookup and3significant-figure result. Give exact direct comparisons wherepossible. Explain one specific circumstance where conversion to simpler arithmetic is useful and one limit of using the rounded tables/domain. A reasoned preference for a different method is acceptable;enthusiasm is not graded.
sections.exemplar: log3²≈2×0.4771=0.9542;inverse≈8.999→9.00to3sig;exact3²=9. log√5≈0.6990/2=0.3495;inverse≈2.236→2.24;exact√5 remains√5. A valid reflection names converting products/quotients/powers/roots toaddition/subtraction/multiplication/division and a concrete precision orpositive-input limit;directarithmetic is preferable forsome simpleexacttasks.
